- **Before editing an existing module:** if `entire graph` is available, run `entire graph impact --symbol <name> --json`.
- **When you finish:** give a short summary covering what you built, the test output, any `src/types.ts` change, and anything unfinished.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

# Roster: design

**Roster is an agent that runs performance reviews for a team's AI coding agents.** It reads every session the team's coding agents recorded with [Entire](https://entire.io), then works out:
- what each session cost
- whether its change survived, was reverted, or was reworked by a human

It then tests its suspicion: it replays the weakest setup's real past tasks under candidate setups, each task at the commit before it with no future history. It promotes a candidate only if nothing regresses, and opens a pull request with the change. Finally it books the team's AI workforce into its [cfo.ai](https://cfo.ai) plan. Every Roster run is traced in [neatlogs](https://neatlogs.com).

This file is the engineering contract for everyone building Roster, humans and agents. Keep to its names and shapes. If you need to change a shared shape, change `src/types.ts` minimally and say so in your PR.

---

## Overview: the loop

```
repo URL
 → Ingest   Entire checkpoints → sessions (setup, model, tokens, prompts, files, commit)
 → Score    survival · reverted · rework (human/agent) · unattended · cost            evidence level A (observational)
 → Review   difficulty-matched scorecard → "suspect: setup X" (Mantel–Haenszel OR, CI, p)
 → Plan     coordinator: stratified task sample, candidates, budget, stop rules
 → Replay   each task at its parent commit in an isolated sandbox; incumbent + candidates
 → Grade    hidden acceptance tests · suite at parent · scope guard · blind diff-judge · reruns
 → Gate     promote only if nothing regresses                                         evidence level B (controlled replay)
     └ reject → Candidates: a new rules file from the failure taxonomy → Replay
 → Act      pull request: setups/<id>.json + rules file + evidence
 → Forward  pre-registered new tasks, paired old vs new, blind grading                evidence level C (forward)
 → Book     cfo.ai: AI Workforce department + hire-vs-scale scenario, read back to verify
```

The rule: a setup is never called "worse" on level A alone. Every page prints the evidence level next to every claim.

## Setups

**Setup** = `harness` + `model` + `rules_hash` (+ `plugins_hash` when recorded).

| Part | Where it comes from |
|---|---|
| `harness` | Entire metadata |
| `model` | The **resolved** model the run reports (e.g. `modelUsage`), never the requested flag |
| `rules_hash` | sha256 of the rules file in effect at the session's parent commit, normalised (LF line endings, trimmed): `CLAUDE.md` for Claude Code, `AGENTS.md` for Codex, `.cursor/rules/*` / `.cursorrules` for Cursor. It also covers any appended system prompt the session records. If unknown, `null`; never a guess |

### The four setups building this repo
These live in `setups/`:

| Id | Harness | Model | Rules |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | Claude Code | Opus 5.5 | `setups/rules/default.md` |
| B | Claude Code | Sonnet 5.5 | default |
| C | Codex CLI (or Claude Code + Haiku 5.5, if Codex is unavailable; logged in `experiments/PREREGISTRATION.md`) | | default (as `AGENTS.md`) |
| D | Claude Code | Sonnet 5.5 | `setups/rules/strict.md` |

### Self-build protocol
This is what makes this repo a labelled dataset.
1. **Task ids and assignment.** Every build task has an id `Txx` and a seeded random setup assignment (seed `20261010`). Both are published in `experiments/PREREGISTRATION.md`.
2. **Prompt tag.** The first prompt of every session starts with `[roster setup=<id> task=<Txx>]`. Roster's own setup inference is checked against these tags.
3. **One task per worktree.** One task gets one worktree and one branch, launched by `scripts/run-setup.sh <setup> <task>` with isolated settings: `--setting-sources project --strict-mcp-config`. The project `.mcp.json` holds only Entire and neatlogs.
4. **Merging.** Merge with `git merge --no-ff`. **Never squash**: squashing drops the `Entire-Checkpoint` trailers that attribution depends on.
5. **Commit prefixes.** Human fixes are separate commits prefixed `human:`. Operational work is prefixed `ops:` and excluded from every experiment.

## Entire checkpoint format

This section was verified on 2026-10-10 against 6 public repos (2,421 session rows). Redacted real samples are in `tests/fixtures/samples/`. Build against them.

### Two storage backends (read both)

| Backend | Where | Layout | Checkpoint id |
|---|---|---|---|
| `branch` (legacy, visible on GitHub) | `refs/heads/entire/checkpoints/v1`, one cumulative tree | `<id[0:2]>/<id[2:]>/…` | 12 hex chars, e.g. `02674b7ab946` → `02/674b7ab946/` |
| `git-refs` (default since CLI 0.10) | One ref per checkpoint: `refs/entire/checkpoints/<id[-2:]>/<id>` | The ref commit's tree root is the checkpoint | 26-char ULID (12-hex ids also occur) |

- An empty `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch means the repo migrated to refs, so always try both backends.
- On refs, the ref commit's message carries the trailers `Checkpoint: <id>`, `Entire-Session: <uuid>`, `Entire-Strategy: manual-commit|import` and `Entire-Agent: <name>`.
- Commits on code branches link to a checkpoint with the trailer `Entire-Checkpoint: <id>`.

### The tree of one checkpoint

```
metadata.json                 checkpoint root: cli_version, checkpoint_id, strategy, branch, files_touched, sessions[], token_usage
<n>/metadata.json             one per session in this checkpoint (n = 0, 1, …)
<n>/full.jsonl                the agent's native transcript (best-effort redacted)
<n>/transcript.jsonl          Entire's compact transcript (CLI ≥ 0.10)
<n>/prompt.txt                user prompts joined by "\n\n---\n\n" (sometimes missing)
<n>/content_hash.txt          "sha256:<hex>" of full.jsonl
tasks/<tool_use_id>/          subagents: task.json, agent-<id>.jsonl
```

- Paths in the root `sessions[]` are repo-absolute on the branch backend (`/02/674b7ab946/0/metadata.json`). Normalise them.

### Session `metadata.json`: the keys we use

| Key | Notes |
|---|---|
| `session_id` | The agent's own id. **The same session recurs across checkpoints.** Aggregate per session over all its checkpoints |
| `agent` | Display name: `Claude Code`, `Codex`, `Copilot CLI`, `Factory AI Droid`, `Pi`, … |
| `model` | Often `""`. Fall back to the transcript (below) |
| `created_at` | RFC3339; roughly the commit time |

| `files_touched[]` | Repo-relative paths |
| `initial_attribution.{agent_lines, agent_removed, human_added, human_modified, human_removed, total_committed, agent_percentage}` | Entire's own agent-vs-human line attribution for the commit |
| `prompt_attributions[]` | Per-prompt line attribution, when present |
| `session_metrics.turn_count`, `strategy`, `branch`, `cli_version` | `strategy: "import"` marks history imported from before capture. Exclude it from any event-period analysis |

- **Not recorded:** cost, a rules-file hash, the harness version (except inside transcripts), and the parent commit.

### Recovering the model and the rules file from transcripts

- **Claude Code `full.jsonl`:**
  - `type:"assistant"` lines carry `.message.model` and `.message.usage{input_tokens, cache_creation_input_tokens, cache_read_input_tokens, output_tokens}`.
  - `type:"attachment"` with `attachment.type:"model"` carries `identity.modelId`, e.g. `claude-opus-5-5[1m]`.
  - `attachment.type:"instructions"` (`files[].{path,type,content}`) and `"nested_memory"` carry the **full text of the CLAUDE.md files loaded**. That's the rules file. Hash the `type: Project` entries.
- **Codex `full.jsonl`:**
  - `turn_context.payload.model`
  - `world_state.payload.state.agents_md` (AGENTS.md)
  - `event_msg` with `payload.type:"token_count"` gives `info.total_token_usage{input_tokens, cached_input_tokens, cache_write_input_tokens, output_tokens, reasoning_output_tokens}`
- **Copilot CLI and Factory Droid:** they record neither model nor tokens, so `cost = null` and the model is `unknown`.
- **Rules-file fallback:** hash `CLAUDE.md` / `AGENTS.md` at the parent of the session's first linked commit.

### Mapping recipe
1. List checkpoints from both backends.
2. Map each checkpoint to its commit through the `Entire-Checkpoint:` trailers on all branches.
3. For each `<n>/metadata.json`: `(session_id, checkpoint_id)` gives the token slice and the files.
4. Group by `session_id` to get one Session. Its tokens are the sum of its slices, and its commits are the set of linked commits.
5. Model: `metadata.model` if it isn't empty, otherwise the transcript.
6. The rules hash comes from the transcript attachments, otherwise from the parent-commit fallback.
7. The setup is `(agent, model, rules_hash)`.

## Architecture

| `initial_attribution.{agent_lines, agent_removed, human_added, human_modified, human_removed, total_committed, agent_percentage}` | Entire's own agent-vs-human line attribution for the commit |
| `prompt_attributions[]` | Per-prompt line attribution, when present |
| `session_metrics.turn_count`, `strategy`, `branch`, `cli_version` | `strategy: "import"` marks history imported from before capture. Exclude it from any event-period analysis |

- **Not recorded:** cost, a rules-file hash, the harness version (except inside transcripts), and the parent commit.

### Recovering the model and the rules file from transcripts

- **Claude Code `full.jsonl`:**
  - `type:"assistant"` lines carry `.message.model` and `.message.usage{input_tokens, cache_creation_input_tokens, cache_read_input_tokens, output_tokens}`.
  - `type:"attachment"` with `attachment.type:"model"` carries `identity.modelId`, e.g. `claude-opus-5-5[1m]`.
  - `attachment.type:"instructions"` (`files[].{path,type,content}`) and `"nested_memory"` carry the **full text of the CLAUDE.md files loaded**. That's the rules file. Hash the `type: Project` entries.
- **Codex `full.jsonl`:**
  - `turn_context.payload.model`
  - `world_state.payload.state.agents_md` (AGENTS.md)
  - `event_msg` with `payload.type:"token_count"` gives `info.total_token_usage{input_tokens, cached_input_tokens, cache_write_input_tokens, output_tokens, reasoning_output_tokens}`
- **Copilot CLI and Factory Droid:** they record neither model nor tokens, so `cost = null` and the model is `unknown`.
- **Rules-file fallback:** hash `CLAUDE.md` / `AGENTS.md` at the parent of the session's first linked commit.

### Mapping recipe
1. List checkpoints from both backends.
2. Map each checkpoint to its commit through the `Entire-Checkpoint:` trailers on all branches.
3. For each `<n>/metadata.json`: `(session_id, checkpoint_id)` gives the token slice and the files.
4. Group by `session_id` to get one Session. Its tokens are the sum of its slices, and its commits are the set of linked commits.
5. Model: `metadata.model` if it isn't empty, otherwise the transcript.
6. The rules hash comes from the transcript attachments, otherwise from the parent-commit fallback.
7. The setup is `(agent, model, rules_hash)`.

127	## Features and acceptance
128	
129	### Ingest
130	- **What it does:**
131	  - Partial clone (`--filter=blob:none`).
132	  - Fetch the `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch. If it's missing, fetch `refs/entire/checkpoints/*`. If neither exists, report "no Entire data" with a one-line how-to.
133	  - Parse each checkpoint into `Session` rows.
134	  - Map each checkpoint to its commit through the trailers on all branches.
135	  - Multi-session checkpoints become separate sessions. Subagent tasks attach to their parent. Sessions with no commit are kept with `commit_sha = null`. A commit with no trailer counts as human.
136	  - `n_user_prompts` excludes tool approvals.
137	- **Done when:**
138	  - it parses this repo plus 3 public repos
139	  - setup inference matches the prompt tags in ≥ 95% of sessions
140	  - a 300-session repo ingests in ≤ 60 s
141	
142	### Score
143	Only *mature* sessions are scored: the commit is ≥ 5 first-parent commits **and** ≥ 6 h older than HEAD. Others are `too_young` with null metrics.
144	
145	| Metric | Definition |
146	|---|---|
147	| `survival` | Lines the session's commit(s) added that `git blame -w -M -C HEAD` still attributes to them ÷ lines added. Whitespace-only and generated files (lockfiles, `dist/`, `*.min.*`) are ignored |
148	| `reverted` | A later commit says `This reverts commit <sha>`, **or** ≥ 50% of the added lines are deleted within the next 20 first-parent commits |
149	| `rework_human` / `rework_agent` | The share of added lines modified within 20 commits by commits without / with a checkpoint trailer |
150	| `unattended` | The session needed exactly one user prompt |
151	| `cost_usd` | Σ tokens by type × `src/price/prices.json`. Every row carries a source URL and date. An unknown model gives `null` |
152	| `cost_per_surviving_change` | Σ cost ÷ Σ survival, per setup |
153	
154	### Difficulty and review
155	- **Difficulty** `d(s)`: the mean z-score of these, then split into terciles:
156	  - `log(1 + lines changed)`
157	  - files touched
158	  - graph impact size: `entire graph impact --symbol <s> --json` over the symbols in the touched hunks, or import fan-in when the graph is unavailable (the method used is recorded)
159	  - the length of the first prompt
160	- **Suspect:** the Mantel–Haenszel odds ratio for `bad = reverted ∨ rework_human > 0.3`, setup X vs the rest, stratified by tercile, with a 95% CI and p.
161	  - It needs ≥ 8 mature sessions for X. Otherwise the result is `insufficient data`.
162	  - The only labels are `suspect (level A, observational)`, `no suspect` and `insufficient data`.
163	- **Done when:** on a confounded fixture (X gets only the hard tasks), the raw rates would flag X and the matched comparison does not.
164	
165	### Plan (coordinator)
166	- **The plan** (`plan.json`):
167	  - `suspect`
168	  - `tasks[]`: ≤ 12, stratified by tercile
169	  - `candidates[]`: ≤ 3 per iteration, ≤ 2 iterations
170	  - `budget_usd`
171	  - `stop_rules`
172	  - `rationale`: one paragraph
173	- **A task is eligible when:**
174	  - its session had ≤ 2 user prompts
175	  - the parent commit installs and its suite passes in the sandbox
176	  - hidden acceptance tests exist (otherwise it goes to the judge-only track, which is never used alone for promotion)
177	
178	### Replay at the parent commit
179	- **Sandbox:**
180	  1. `git archive <parent> | tar -x` into a fresh directory.
181	  2. `git init`, then one base commit with a fixed author and date.
182	  3. Isolation proof: zero objects from `git rev-list --objects --all ^<parent>` exist in the sandbox, there are no remotes, a single ref, and no reflog beyond the base.
183	  - Clone + reset is forbidden (it's a denylist and leaks).
184	- **Rules swap:** write the setup's rules file into the sandbox and commit it as `setup:`, so the agent's diff excludes it.
185	- **Harness adapters** (`src/harness/*`, one contract):
186	  - **Claude Code:**
187	    ```
188	    claude -p "<task>" --model <m> --output-format json --max-turns 30
189	      --permission-mode acceptEdits --permission-prompts none --allowedTools "<allowlist>"
190	      --setting-sources project --strict-mcp-config --disable-slash-commands --max-budget-usd <cap>
191	    ```
192	    The child env is scrubbed of host-session variables.
193	    JSON fields: `session_id, num_turns, duration_ms, total_cost_usd, usage, modelUsage, is_error, stop_reason`.
194	  - **Codex:**
195	    ```
196	    codex exec --json --model <m> --sandbox workspace-write -c approval_policy=never -C <ws> "<task>"
197	    ```
198	    Rules go in `AGENTS.md`. Tokens come from `turn.completed.usage`; it reports no USD (price it via `src/price`) and has no turn cap (use a wall-clock timeout).
199	- **Save:** `agent.patch` (`git diff --binary`) and the raw JSON or stream-json transcript.
200	- **Where replays run:** replays of public repos run only in isolated microVMs. Replays of this repo may run locally.
201	
202	### Grade
203	1. **Grade in a separate copy:** base + `agent.patch` + hidden tests. Never grade in the agent's workspace.
204	2. **Hidden tests:** the test files the original change added or modified, taken from the commit where those lines matured. That's the version the team accepted.
205	3. **Run:** the agent's suite, then the full suite with per-test JUnit written outside the workspace. A hidden file that collects 0 tests counts as a failing case (bun's JUnit reporter silently drops files that fail to import).
206	4. **Scope guard:** pre-existing test cases are unmodified (appending new cases is allowed), no files outside the touched-directory set change, and typecheck and lint pass if configured.
207	5. **Blind diff-judge:** compares the two diffs under random labels. It's advisory.
208	6. **Disagreement:** if the grader and the judge disagree, or two setups split on a task, rerun it, up to k = 3, majority wins.
209	7. **Failure taxonomy:**
210	
211	| Code | Failure |
212	|---|---|
213	| F1 | edited tests |
214	| F2 | never ran tests |
215	| F3 | suite regression |
216	| F4 | stopped early |
217	| F5 | loop, timeout or turn cap |
218	| F6 | environment or setup error. The task is excluded and resampled |
219	| F7 | off-scope edits |
220	
221	**Verdict order:** `agent_error` > `no_changes` > `hidden_tests_failed` > `suite_failed` > guardrail flags > `pass`.
222	
223	### Gate (deterministic code; the coordinator can't override it)
224	
225	```
226	promote(candidate) iff, on the replay set (incumbent replayed as the control):
227	  hidden_pass(candidate) ≥ hidden_pass(incumbent)
228	  ∧ regressions == 0          # tasks the incumbent passed and the candidate failed, after reruns
229	  ∧ scope_violations == 0
230	  ∧ cost(candidate) ≤ budget
231	ties → cheaper wins; still tied → keep incumbent
232	```
233	
234	- **Every rejection** writes `{candidate, failed_tasks, reasons, trace_url}`.
235	- **If no candidate passes,** the result is "no better setup found". That is a valid outcome.
236	
237	### Candidate generation
238	- **The candidates are:**
239	  - the other existing setups
240	  - rules mutations: X's harness and model with the rules file patched from X's top failure codes, using `src/candidates/rules-lib.md`. For example:
241	    - F2 → "run the full test suite before you finish"
242	    - F1 → "never modify existing tests unless asked"
243	- **Traceability:** every added rule cites the failure codes it answers.
244	
245	### Act
246	- **On our own repo:** a PR with `setups/<id>.json`, the rules file, the review summary, an evidence table, neatlogs trace links and entire.io links.
247	- **On other people's repos:** never unsolicited. Only for teams that opted in.
248	
249	### Observability (neatlogs)
250	- **Trace structure:** a `WORKFLOW review` root, then `AGENT coordinator`, then `TOOL` spans (one per ingest, score, replay attempt, grade and cfo.ai write), plus a `GUARDRAIL gate` span.
251	- **Attributes:** `roster.setup, roster.task, roster.attempt, roster.failure_code, roster.evidence_level, roster.repo, roster.cost_usd`.
252	- **Session:** `identify(session_id = review_id)`.
253	- **Detections:**
254	
255	| Detection | Fires when |
256	|---|---|
257	| D1 silent pass | The visible suite passed, but hidden acceptance or the scope guard failed |
258	| D2 low attribution confidence | More than 30% of a setup's lines are unmapped |
259	| D3 cost anomaly | Cost exceeds 3× the incumbent median |
260	| D4 environment flake | F6 hits the same task across ≥ 2 setups |
261	
262	- **No API key:** with `NEATLOGS_API_KEY` unset, observability is a no-op with one warning.
263	
264	### Book (cfo.ai)
265	- **Writes over the cfo.ai MCP:**
266	  - an **AI Workforce** department: monthly spend per setup, surviving changes, cost per surviving change, unattended %
267	  - a **Hire 1 engineer vs scale the promoted setup** scenario
268	- **Verify:** read the blocks back and diff them against `book.json`. A mismatch means retry once, then report it.
269	
270	### Forward run (pre-registered)
271	- **Registration:** the backlog (`experiments/forward-backlog.md`) and its acceptance tests (`experiments/acceptance/`) are committed, and their sha256 is published, **before** the review that picks the setups.
272	- **The acceptance tests** are written by a separate agent from the task text alone, before either setup runs.
273	- **Each task runs through both setups** in paired worktrees from the same main commit.
274	- **Grading is blind** (random X/Y labels).
275	- **Merge policy:** pass beats fail. If both pass, the blind judge's preference wins. If the judge ties, a random pick with a logged seed. Merge with `--no-ff`.
276	- **Statistics:** McNemar exact (two-sided, α = 0.05) on the pairs, and Wilcoxon signed-rank on cost.
277	- **Stop rule:** after ≥ 15 pairs, if the promoted setup has lost at least 3 more discordant pairs than it has won, open a revert PR and continue on the old setup.
278	- **Invalidated tasks** are excluded for both setups, with a reason.

| `reverted` | A later commit says `This reverts commit <sha>`, **or** ≥ 50% of the added lines are deleted within the next 20 first-parent commits |
| `rework_human` / `rework_agent` | The share of added lines modified within 20 commits by commits without / with a checkpoint trailer |
| `unattended` | The session needed exactly one user prompt |
| `cost_usd` | Σ tokens by type × `src/price/prices.json`. Every row carries a source URL and date. An unknown model gives `null` |
| `cost_per_surviving_change` | Σ cost ÷ Σ survival, per setup |

### Difficulty and review
- **Difficulty** `d(s)`: the mean z-score of these, then split into terciles:
  - `log(1 + lines changed)`
  - files touched
  - graph impact size: `entire graph impact --symbol <s> --json` over the symbols in the touched hunks, or import fan-in when the graph is unavailable (the method used is recorded)
  - the length of the first prompt
- **Suspect:** the Mantel–Haenszel odds ratio for `bad = reverted ∨ rework_human > 0.3`, setup X vs the rest, stratified by tercile, with a 95% CI and p.
  - It needs ≥ 8 mature sessions for X. Otherwise the result is `insufficient data`.
  - The only labels are `suspect (level A, observational)`, `no suspect` and `insufficient data`.
- **Done when:** on a confounded fixture (X gets only the hard tasks), the raw rates would flag X and the matched comparison does not.

### Plan (coordinator)
- **The plan** (`plan.json`):
  - `suspect`
  - `tasks[]`: ≤ 12, stratified by tercile
  - `candidates[]`: ≤ 3 per iteration, ≤ 2 iterations
  - `budget_usd`
  - `stop_rules`
  - `rationale`: one paragraph
- **A task is eligible when:**
  - its session had ≤ 2 user prompts
  - the parent commit installs and its suite passes in the sandbox
  - hidden acceptance tests exist (otherwise it goes to the judge-only track, which is never used alone for promotion)

### Replay at the parent commit
- **Sandbox:**
  1. `git archive <parent> | tar -x` into a fresh directory.
  2. `git init`, then one base commit with a fixed author and date.
  3. Isolation proof: zero objects from `git rev-list --objects --all ^<parent>` exist in the sandbox, there are no remotes, a single ref, and no reflog beyond the base.
  - Clone + reset is forbidden (it's a denylist and leaks).
- **Rules swap:** write the setup's rules file into the sandbox and commit it as `setup:`, so the agent's diff excludes it.
- **Harness adapters** (`src/harness/*`, one contract):
  - **Claude Code:**
    ```
    claude -p "<task>" --model <m> --output-format json --max-turns 30
      --permission-mode acceptEdits --permission-prompts none --allowedTools "<allowlist>"
      --setting-sources project --strict-mcp-config --disable-slash-commands --max-budget-usd <cap>
    ```
    The child env is scrubbed of host-session variables.
    JSON fields: `session_id, num_turns, duration_ms, total_cost_usd, usage, modelUsage, is_error, stop_reason`.
  - **Codex:**
    ```
    codex exec --json --model <m> --sandbox workspace-write -c approval_policy=never -C <ws> "<task>"
    ```
    Rules go in `AGENTS.md`. Tokens come from `turn.completed.usage`; it reports no USD (price it via `src/price`) and has no turn cap (use a wall-clock timeout).
- **Save:** `agent.patch` (`git diff --binary`) and the raw JSON or stream-json transcript.
- **Where replays run:** replays of public repos run only in isolated microVMs. Replays of this repo may run locally.

### Grade
1. **Grade in a separate copy:** base + `agent.patch` + hidden tests. Never grade in the agent's workspace.
2. **Hidden tests:** the test files the original change added or modified, taken from the commit where those lines matured. That's the version the team accepted.
3. **Run:** the agent's suite, then the full suite with per-test JUnit written outside the workspace. A hidden file that collects 0 tests counts as a failing case (bun's JUnit reporter silently drops files that fail to import).
4. **Scope guard:** pre-existing test cases are unmodified (appending new cases is allowed), no files outside the touched-directory set change, and typecheck and lint pass if configured.
5. **Blind diff-judge:** compares the two diffs under random labels. It's advisory.
6. **Disagreement:** if the grader and the judge disagree, or two setups split on a task, rerun it, up to k = 3, majority wins.
7. **Failure taxonomy:**

| Code | Failure |
|---|---|
| F1 | edited tests |
| F2 | never ran tests |
| F3 | suite regression |
| F4 | stopped early |
| F5 | loop, timeout or turn cap |
| F6 | environment or setup error. The task is excluded and resampled |
| F7 | off-scope edits |

**Verdict order:** `agent_error` > `no_changes` > `hidden_tests_failed` > `suite_failed` > guardrail flags > `pass`.

### Gate (deterministic code; the coordinator can't override it)

```
promote(candidate) iff, on the replay set (incumbent replayed as the control):
  hidden_pass(candidate) ≥ hidden_pass(incumbent)
  ∧ regressions == 0          # tasks the incumbent passed and the candidate failed, after reruns
  ∧ scope_violations == 0
  ∧ cost(candidate) ≤ budget
ties → cheaper wins; still tied → keep incumbent
```

- **Every rejection** writes `{candidate, failed_tasks, reasons, trace_url}`.
- **If no candidate passes,** the result is "no better setup found". That is a valid outcome.

### Candidate generation
- **The candidates are:**
  - the other existing setups
  - rules mutations: X's harness and model with the rules file patched from X's top failure codes, using `src/candidates/rules-lib.md`. For example:
    - F2 → "run the full test suite before you finish"
    - F1 → "never modify existing tests unless asked"
- **Traceability:** every added rule cites the failure codes it answers.

### Act
- **On our own repo:** a PR with `setups/<id>.json`, the rules file, the review summary, an evidence table, neatlogs trace links and entire.io links.
- **On other people's repos:** never unsolicited. Only for teams that opted in.

### Observability (neatlogs)
- **Trace structure:** a `WORKFLOW review` root, then `AGENT coordinator`, then `TOOL` spans (one per ingest, score, replay attempt, grade and cfo.ai write), plus a `GUARDRAIL gate` span.
- **Attributes:** `roster.setup, roster.task, roster.attempt, roster.failure_code, roster.evidence_level, roster.repo, roster.cost_usd`.
- **Session:** `identify(session_id = review_id)`.
- **Detections:**

| Detection | Fires when |
|---|---|
| D1 silent pass | The visible suite passed, but hidden acceptance or the scope guard failed |
| D2 low attribution confidence | More than 30% of a setup's lines are unmapped |
| D3 cost anomaly | Cost exceeds 3× the incumbent median |
| D4 environment flake | F6 hits the same task across ≥ 2 setups |

- **No API key:** with `NEATLOGS_API_KEY` unset, observability is a no-op with one warning.

### Book (cfo.ai)
- **Writes over the cfo.ai MCP:**
  - an **AI Workforce** department: monthly spend per setup, surviving changes, cost per surviving change, unattended %
  - a **Hire 1 engineer vs scale the promoted setup** scenario
- **Verify:** read the blocks back and diff them against `book.json`. A mismatch means retry once, then report it.

### Forward run (pre-registered)
- **Registration:** the backlog (`experiments/forward-backlog.md`) and its acceptance tests (`experiments/acceptance/`) are committed, and their sha256 is published, **before** the review that picks the setups.
- **The acceptance tests** are written by a separate agent from the task text alone, before either setup runs.
- **Each task runs through both setups** in paired worktrees from the same main commit.
- **Grading is blind** (random X/Y labels).
- **Merge policy:** pass beats fail. If both pass, the blind judge's preference wins. If the judge ties, a random pick with a logged seed. Merge with `--no-ff`.
- **Statistics:** McNemar exact (two-sided, α = 0.05) on the pairs, and Wilcoxon signed-rank on cost.
- **Stop rule:** after ≥ 15 pairs, if the promoted setup has lost at least 3 more discordant pairs than it has won, open a revert PR and continue on the old setup.
- **Invalidated tasks** are excluded for both setups, with a reason.

T01 is done: the acceptance command builds the repo, `bun test tests/types.test.ts` passes (14 tests), and the whole suite passes with no regressions (16 tests across 2 files). Typecheck is clean. There are three commits, all prefixed `T01:`.

**What I built**
- **`src/types.ts`** (new file): `Session`, `Outcome`, `Setup`, `Plan`, `Replay`, `GateDecision`, `ForwardPair` and `Review` follow the DESIGN.md data model. It also has `FailureCode` (F1–F7) and `EvidenceLevel` (`'A'|'B'|'C'`). I added a few small helper types: `PlanBody` for the `plan.json` contents, plus types for verdicts, status and tercile. The data model doesn't list fields for `Review`, so I took them from §"Difficulty and review": the label, the suspect setup, the odds ratio, the 95% interval, p and the evidence level.
- **`tests/fixtures/make-fixture.ts`**: run it as `bun tests/fixtures/make-fixture.ts /tmp/fx --scenario basic`.
  - **Payloads:** every checkpoint file is a copy of a real sample with only the values changed, so no new keys appear. Paths in the root `sessions[]` are repo-absolute, as on the real branch.
  - **Three fake setups:**
    - **X:** Claude Code + Opus 5.5 + default rules.
    - **Y:** Claude Code + Sonnet 5.5 + strict rules. Its metadata `model` is `""`, so the model has to come from the transcript.
    - **Z:** Codex, with `AGENTS.md` as its rules file.
  - **Token counts** in the metadata add up to what the transcripts show, and each `content_hash.txt` is the real sha256 of its `full.jsonl`.
  - **Basic scenario:** 12 commits, 4 `Entire-Checkpoint` trailers and one real `git revert`. One human commit without a trailer reworks lines an agent added. One checkpoint holds two sessions, and one session appears in two checkpoints.
  - **Other scenarios:**
    - `confound`: X gets only large changes, and whether a change is reverted depends on its size, not its setup.
    - `revert`: adds a deletion of at least half an agent change's lines, with no revert message.
    - `multisession`: has a checkpoint with three sessions, plus a checkpoint no commit links to.
  - **Determinism:** dates, author and ids are fixed and global git config is ignored, so rebuilding gives the same commit ids (a test checks this).
  - **Answer key:** the script prints which commit and session belongs to which setup to stdout, and saves it to `<outDir>/.git/roster-fixture.json`.
- **`tests/types.test.ts`** checks the acceptance points:
  - file names and top-level JSON keys match the samples, for the checkpoint root, each session's metadata (Claude Code and Codex) and transcript lines
  - 12 commits, 4 trailers and 1 revert
  - each trailer points to a checkpoint that exists on the branch
  - the rework commit, the two-session checkpoint, determinism, and each of the other scenarios

**Things to know**
- **No change to `tests/fixtures/samples/`:** I didn't add or edit any samples.
- **Only the legacy storage:** the builder writes checkpoints to the `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch only, not to the one-ref-per-checkpoint (`git-refs`) storage. There are no `transcript.jsonl` or subagent `tasks/` files, because no real samples of them exist to copy.
- **Codex rules:** there's no sample of the Codex transcript line that records `AGENTS.md`, so Z's rules can only be recovered from `AGENTS.md` at the parent commit, not from its transcript.
- **Branch commit messages** copy the format of the one real sample, which comes from the other storage backend. I have no sample of a branch commit message.
- **Speed:** `confound` takes about 4 seconds to build, so the test file raises bun's default timeout to 30 seconds.
- **Overwriting:** the script deletes and rebuilds an output folder only if it holds an earlier fixture; for any other non-empty folder it stops unless you pass `--force`.
- **Leftover files:** `/tmp/fx` and `/tmp/fx-confound` from my manual runs are still there.
